+def _tool_choice_to_tool_config(tool_choice: Any) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
+    """Translate an OpenAI ``tool_choice`` into a Gemini ``toolConfig``.
+
+    Returns None for an omitted or ``"auto"`` choice so Gemini keeps its default (AUTO) mode.
+    Docs: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling#function_calling_modes
+    """
+    match tool_choice:
+        case None | "auto":
+            return None
+        case "none":
+            mode_config = {"mode": "NONE"}
+        case "required":
+            mode_config = {"mode": "ANY"}
+        case {"type": "function", "function": {"name": str(name)}}:
+            mode_config = {"mode": "ANY", "allowedFunctionNames": [name]}
+        case _:
+            raise AIGatewayException(
+                status_code=422, detail=f"Unsupported tool_choice value: {tool_choice!r}"
+            )
+    return {"functionCallingConfig": mode_config}

56	def _to_gemini_parts(content: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
57	    """Translate a user message's content into Gemini ``parts``.
58	
59	    A string becomes a single text part (unchanged behavior). A multimodal list has each
60	    part translated: text -> ``{"text": ...}``, ``image_url`` base64 data URL ->
61	    ``{"inlineData": {"mimeType": ..., "data": ...}}``. Non-base64 image URLs fall back to
62	    a text note since the judge image tool only ever emits base64 data URLs. Any other part
63	    type is passed through unchanged rather than coerced to empty text, so a non-text part
64	    (e.g. ``input_audio``) isn't silently dropped.
65	    """
66	    if not isinstance(content, list):
67	        return [{"text": content}]
68	
69	    parts: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
70	    for part in content:
71	        if part.get("type") == "text":
72	            parts.append({"text": part.get("text", "")})
73	        elif part.get("type") == "image_url":
74	            url = part.get("image_url", {}).get("url", "")
75	            if parsed := parse_base64_data_url(url):
76	                mime, data = parsed
77	                parts.append({"inlineData": {"mimeType": mime, "data": data}})
78	            else:
79	                parts.append({"text": f"[unsupported image reference: {url}]"})
80	        else:
81	            parts.append(part)
82	    return parts

85	def _tool_result_to_response(content: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
86	    """Coerce OpenAI tool message content into a Gemini ``functionResponse.response``.
87	
88	    OpenAI tool content is free-form and usually plain text, but Gemini requires an object,
89	    so a JSON object passes through and anything else is wrapped as ``{"result": ...}``.
90	    """
91	    try:
92	        parsed = json.loads(content)
93	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
94	        return {"result": content}
95	    return parsed if isinstance(parsed, dict) else {"result": parsed}

98	def _tool_choice_to_tool_config(tool_choice: Any) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
99	    """Translate an OpenAI ``tool_choice`` into a Gemini ``toolConfig``.
100	
101	    Returns None for an omitted or ``"auto"`` choice so Gemini keeps its default (AUTO) mode.
102	    Docs: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling#function_calling_modes
103	    """
104	    match tool_choice:
105	        case None | "auto":
106	            return None
107	        case "none":
108	            mode_config = {"mode": "NONE"}
109	        case "required":
110	            mode_config = {"mode": "ANY"}
111	        case {"type": "function", "function": {"name": str(name)}}:
112	            mode_config = {"mode": "ANY", "allowedFunctionNames": [name]}
113	        case _:
114	            raise AIGatewayException(
115	                status_code=422, detail=f"Unsupported tool_choice value: {tool_choice!r}"
116	            )
117	    return {"functionCallingConfig": mode_config}

130	    @classmethod
131	    def chat_to_model(cls, payload, config):
132	        # Documentation: https://ai.google.dev/api/generate-content
133	        # Example payload for the chat API.
134	        #
135	        # {
136	        #     "contents": [
137	        #         {
138	        #             "role": "user",
139	        #             "parts": [
140	        #                 {
141	        #                     "text": "System: You are an advanced AI Assistant"
142	        #                 }
143	        #             ]
144	        #         },
145	        #         {
146	        #             "role": "user",
147	        #             "parts": [
148	        #                 {
149	        #                     "text": "Please give the code for addition of two numbers"
150	        #                 }
151	        #             ]
152	        #         }
153	        #     ],
154	        #     "generationConfig": {
155	        #         "temperature": 0.1,
156	        #         "topP": 1,
157	        #         "stopSequences": ["\n"],
158	        #         "candidateCount": 1,
159	        #         "maxOutputTokens": 100,
160	        #         "topK": 40
161	        #     }
162	        # }
163	
164	        for k1, k2 in GENERATION_CONFIG_KEY_MAPPING.items():
165	            if k2 in payload:
166	                raise AIGatewayException(
167	                    status_code=422, detail=f"Invalid parameter {k2}. Use {k1} instead."
168	                )
169	
170	        if "max_completion_tokens" in payload:
171	            if "max_tokens" not in payload:
172	                payload["max_tokens"] = payload.pop("max_completion_tokens")
173	
174	        payload = rename_payload_keys(payload, GENERATION_CONFIG_KEY_MAPPING)
175	
176	        contents = []
177	        system_message = None
178	
179	        call_id_to_function_name_map = {}
180	        call_id_to_thought_signature_map = {}
181	
182	        for message in payload["messages"]:
183	            role = message["role"]
184	
185	            if role in ("user", "assistant"):
186	                if role == "assistant":
187	                    role = "model"
188	
189	                gemini_function_calls = []
190	                if role == "model":
191	                    if tool_calls := message.get("tool_calls"):
192	                        for tool_call in tool_calls:
193	                            call_id_to_function_name_map[tool_call["id"]] = tool_call["function"][
194	                                "name"
195	                            ]
196	                            if sig := tool_call.get("thought_signature"):
197	                                call_id_to_thought_signature_map[tool_call["id"]] = sig
198	
199	                            fc = {
200	                                "id": tool_call["id"],
201	                                "name": tool_call["function"]["name"],
202	                                "args": json.loads(tool_call["function"]["arguments"]),
203	                            }
204	                            part = {"functionCall": fc}
205	                            if tool_call["id"] in call_id_to_thought_signature_map:
206	                                part["thoughtSignature"] = call_id_to_thought_signature_map[
207	                                    tool_call["id"]
208	                                ]
209	
210	                            gemini_function_calls.append(part)
211	                if gemini_function_calls:
212	                    contents.append({"role": "model", "parts": gemini_function_calls})
213	                else:
214	                    # _to_gemini_parts translates multimodal list content (e.g. an image_url
215	                    # part) to Gemini parts; string content stays a single text part.
216	                    contents.append({"role": role, "parts": _to_gemini_parts(message["content"])})
217	            elif role == "system":
218	                if system_message is None:
219	                    system_message = {"parts": []}
220	                system_message["parts"].append({"text": message["content"]})
221	            elif role == "tool":
222	                call_id = message["tool_call_id"]
223	                function_response = {
224	                    "functionResponse": {
225	                        "id": call_id,
226	                        # the function name field is required by Gemini request format
227	                        "name": call_id_to_function_name_map[call_id],
228	                        "response": _tool_result_to_response(message["content"]),
229	                    }
230	                }
231	                # OpenAI sends one tool message per parallel call, but Gemini requires the
232	                # responses to all of a model turn's calls in a single user turn.
233	                previous = contents[-1] if contents else None
234	                if (
235	                    previous is not None
236	                    and previous["role"] == "user"
237	                    and previous["parts"]
238	                    and all("functionResponse" in part for part in previous["parts"])
239	                ):
240	                    previous["parts"].append(function_response)
241	                else:
242	                    contents.append({"role": "user", "parts": [function_response]})
243	
244	        gemini_payload = {"contents": contents}
245	
246	        if system_message:
247	            gemini_payload["system_instruction"] = system_message
248	
249	        if generation_config := {k: v for k, v in payload.items() if k in GENERATION_CONFIGS}:
250	            gemini_payload["generationConfig"] = generation_config
251	
252	        # Transform response_format for Gemini structured outputs
253	        if response_format := payload.pop("response_format", None):
254	            response_format_type = response_format.get("type")
255	            if response_format_type == "json_schema" and "json_schema" in response_format:
256	                generation_config = gemini_payload.setdefault("generationConfig", {})
257	                generation_config["responseJsonSchema"] = response_format["json_schema"]["schema"]
258	                generation_config["responseMimeType"] = "application/json"
259	            elif response_format_type == "json_object":
260	                # Gemini constrains output to valid JSON when responseMimeType is set,
261	                # even without an explicit schema.
262	                generation_config = gemini_payload.setdefault("generationConfig", {})
263	                generation_config["responseMimeType"] = "application/json"
264	
265	        # convert tool definition to Gemini format
266	        if tools := payload.pop("tools", None):
267	            function_declarations = []
268	            for tool in tools:
269	                if tool["type"] != "function":
270	                    raise AIGatewayException(
271	                        status_code=422,
272	                        detail=(
273	                            "Only function calling tool is supported, but received tool type "
274	                            f"{tool['type']}"
275	                        ),
276	                    )
277	
278	                tool_function = tool["function"]
279	                function_declarations.append({
280	                    "name": tool_function["name"],
281	                    "description": tool_function["description"],
282	                    "parametersJsonSchema": tool_function["parameters"],
283	                })
284	
285	            gemini_payload["tools"] = [{"functionDeclarations": function_declarations}]
286	
287	            if tool_config := _tool_choice_to_tool_config(payload.get("tool_choice")):
288	                gemini_payload["toolConfig"] = tool_config
289	
290	        return gemini_payload

292	    @classmethod
293	    def _convert_function_call_to_openai_choice(
294	        cls,
295	        content_parts: list[dict[str, Any]],
296	        finish_reason: str,
297	        choice_idx: int,
298	        stream: bool,
299	    ):
300	        # convert gemini model responded "function call" struct to Openai choice / choice chunk
301	        # struct.
302	        # Gemini doc: https://ai.google.dev/api/caching#FunctionCall
303	
304	        # A candidate can mix text and functionCall parts in any order, e.g. a short
305	        # "Let me look that up." followed by the call. Keep both.
306	        tool_calls = []
307	        text_parts = []
308	        for part in content_parts:
309	            if "text" in part:
310	                text_parts.append(part["text"])
311	            function_call = part.get("functionCall")
312	            if not function_call:
313	                continue
314	            func_name = function_call["name"]
315	            func_arguments = json.dumps(function_call["args"])
316	            call_id = function_call.get("id")
317	            # Gemini 3.x places thoughtSignature at the Part level, next to functionCall.
318	            # Some older responses nested it inside functionCall instead, so fall back to
319	            # that location too.
320	            thought_sig = (
321	                part.get("thoughtSignature")
322	                or part.get("thought_signature")
323	                or function_call.get("thoughtSignature")
324	                or function_call.get("thought_signature")
325	            )
326	            if call_id is None:
327	                # Gemini model response might not contain function call id,
328	                # in order to make it compatible with Openai chat protocol,
329	                # we need to generate a unique call id.
330	                call_id = (
331	                    "call_"
332	                    + hashlib.md5(
333	                        f"{func_name}/{func_arguments}".encode(),
334	                        usedforsecurity=False,
335	                    ).hexdigest()
336	                )
337	            if stream:
338	                tool_calls.append(
339	                    chat_schema.ToolCallDelta(
340	                        index=0,
341	                        id=call_id,
342	                        function=Function(
343	                            name=func_name,
344	                            arguments=func_arguments,
345	                        ),
346	                        type="function",
347	                        thought_signature=thought_sig,
348	                    )
349	                )
350	            else:
351	                tool_calls.append(
352	                    ToolCall(
353	                        id=call_id,
354	                        function=Function(
355	                            name=func_name,
356	                            arguments=func_arguments,
357	                        ),
358	                        type="function",
359	                        thought_signature=thought_sig,
360	                    )
361	                )
362	        content = "".join(text_parts) or None
363	        if stream:
364	            return chat_schema.StreamChoice(
365	                index=choice_idx,
366	                delta=chat_schema.StreamDelta(
367	                    role="assistant",
368	                    content=content,
369	                    tool_calls=tool_calls,
370	                ),
371	                finish_reason=finish_reason,
372	            )
373	        return chat_schema.Choice(
374	            index=choice_idx,
375	            message=chat_schema.ResponseMessage(
376	                role="assistant",
377	                content=content,
378	                tool_calls=tool_calls,
379	            ),
380	            finish_reason=finish_reason,
381	        )

388	            if key

406	            prompt_tokens_details=prompt_tokens_details,

409	    @classmethod
410	    def model_to_chat(cls, resp, config):
411	        # Documentation: https://ai.google.dev/api/generate-content
412	        #
413	        # Example Response:
414	        # {
415	        #   "candidates": [
416	        #     {
417	        #       "content": {
418	        #         "parts": [
419	        #           {
420	        #             "text": "Blue is often seen as a calming and soothing color."
421	        #           }
422	        #         ]
423	        #       },
424	        #       "finishReason": "stop"
425	        #     }
426	        #   ],
427	        #   "usageMetadata": {
428	        #     "promptTokenCount": 10,
429	        #     "candidatesTokenCount": 10,
430	        #     "totalTokenCount": 20
431	        #   }
432	        # }
433	        choices = []
434	        for idx, candidate in enumerate(resp.get("candidates", [])):
435	            finish_reason = cls._normalize_finish_reason(candidate.get("finishReason", "stop"))
436	
437	            if parts := candidate.get("content", {}).get("parts", None):
438	                if any(part.get("functionCall") for part in parts):
439	                    choices.append(
440	                        GeminiAdapter._convert_function_call_to_openai_choice(
441	                            parts, finish_reason, idx, False
442	                        )
443	                    )
444	
445	                elif content := parts[0].get("text"):
446	                    choices.append(
447	                        chat_schema.Choice(
448	                            index=idx,
449	                            message=chat_schema.ResponseMessage(
450	                                role="assistant",
451	                                content=content,
452	                            ),
453	                            finish_reason=finish_reason,
454	                        )
455	                    )
456	
457	        usage_metadata = resp.get("usageMetadata", {})
458	
459	        return chat_schema.ResponsePayload(
460	            id=f"gemini-chat-{int(time.time())}",
461	            created=int(time.time()),
462	            object="chat.completion",
463	            model=config.model.name,
464	            choices=choices,
465	            usage=cls._build_chat_usage(usage_metadata),
466	        )

469	    def model_to_chat_streaming(
470	        cls, resp: dict[str, Any], config
471	    ) -> chat_schema.StreamResponsePayload:
472	        # Documentation: https://ai.google.dev/api/generate-content#method:-models.streamgeneratecontent
473	        #
474	        # Example Streaming Chunk:
475	        # {
476	        #   "candidates": [
477	        #     {
478	        #       "content": {
479	        #         "parts": [
480	        #           {
481	        #             "text": "Blue is often seen as a calming and soothing color."
482	        #           }
483	        #         ]
484	        #       },
485	        #       "finishReason": null
486	        #     }
487	        #   ],
488	        #   "id": "stream-id",
489	        #   "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
490	        #   "created": 1234567890,
491	        #   "model": "gemini-2.0-flash"
492	        # }
493	        choices = []
494	        for idx, cand in enumerate(resp.get("candidates", [])):
495	            parts = cand.get("content", {}).get("parts", [])
496	            finish_reason = cls._normalize_finish_reason(cand.get("finishReason"))
497	
498	            if parts:
499	                if any(part.get("functionCall") for part in parts):
500	                    # for gemini model streaming response,
501	                    # the function call message is not split into chunks
502	                    # it still contains the full function call arguments data.
503	                    choices.append(
504	                        GeminiAdapter._convert_function_call_to_openai_choice(
505	                            parts, finish_reason, idx, True
506	                        )
507	                    )
508	                    continue
509	
510	            delta_text = parts[0].get("text", "") if parts else ""
511	            choices.append(
512	                chat_schema.StreamChoice(
513	                    index=idx,
514	                    finish_reason=finish_reason,
515	                    delta=chat_schema.StreamDelta(
516	                        role="assistant",
517	                        content=delta_text,
518	                    ),
519	                )
520	            )
521	        current_time = int(time.time())
522	
523	        # Extract usage from usageMetadata (available in final chunk)
524	        usage = None
525	        if usage_metadata := resp.get("usageMetadata"):
526	            usage = cls._build_chat_usage(usage_metadata)
527	
528	        return chat_schema.StreamResponsePayload(
529	            id=f"gemini-chat-stream-{current_time}",
530	            object="chat.completion.chunk",
531	            created=current_time,
532	            model=config.model.name,
533	            choices=choices,
534	            usage=usage,
535	        )

939	        """

941

943	        {
944	            "usageMetadata": {
945	                "promptTokenCount": int,
946	                "candidatesTokenCount": int,
947	                "totalTokenCount": int
948	            }
949	        }
950	        """
951	        usage_metadata = result.get("usageMetadata")
952	        return self._extract_token_usage_from_dict(

954	            "promptTokenCount",
955	            "candidatesTokenCount",

960	    def _extract_streaming_token_usage(self, chunk: bytes) -> dict[str, int]:
961	        """
962	        Extract token usage from Gemini streaming chunks.
963	
964	        Gemini streaming format uses SSE with usageMetadata in chunks (typically final chunk):
965	        data: {"candidates": [...], "usageMetadata": {"promptTokenCount": X, ...}}
966	
967	        Returns:
968	            A dictionary with token usage found in this chunk.
969	        """
970	        try:
971	            chunk_str = chunk.decode("utf-8").strip()
972	            if not chunk_str:
973	                return {}
974	
975	            # Parse SSE format - look for data lines
976	            for line in chunk_str.split("\n"):
977	                line = line.strip()
978	                if not line.startswith("data:"):
979	                    continue
980	
981	                data_str = line[5:].strip()
982	                if not data_str or data_str == "[DONE]":
983	                    continue
984	
985	                data = json.loads(data_str)
986	
987	                # Extract usageMetadata if present
988	                usage_metadata = data.get("usageMetadata")
989	                if token_usage := self._extract_token_usage_from_dict(
990	                    usage_metadata,
991	                    "promptTokenCount",
992	                    "candidatesTokenCount",
993	                    "totalTokenCount",
994	                    cache_read_key="cachedContentTokenCount",
995	                ):
996	                    return token_usage
997	
998	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError):
999	            pass
1000	
1001	        return {}

669	def test_claude_adapter_applies_vertex_fields_without_provider_hooks():
670	    """Formatting through ``adapter_class`` alone must produce a Vertex-valid payload.
671	
672	    ``_prepare_payload`` is a provider hook reached only from ``AnthropicProvider._chat``
673	    and ``._chat_stream``. Callers that build a request from the adapter and post it
674	    themselves -- the judge path in ``mlflow.genai.judges.adapters.gateway_adapter``
675	    does exactly this -- never run that hook, so Vertex rejected the request with
676	    "anthropic_version: Field required". The transformation therefore has to live on the
677	    adapter, as it already does for Bedrock.
678	    """
679	    from mlflow.gateway.providers.vertex_ai import _VERTEX_ANTHROPIC_VERSION
680	
681	    provider = _make_claude_provider()
682	    payload = {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}], "max_tokens": 16}
683	
684	    formatted = provider.adapter_class.chat_to_model(dict(payload), provider.config)
685	    assert formatted["anthropic_version"] == _VERTEX_ANTHROPIC_VERSION
686	    # Vertex carries the model in the URL and rejects it in the body.
687	    assert "model" not in formatted
688	
689	    streamed = provider.adapter_class.chat_streaming_to_model(dict(payload), provider.config)
690	    assert streamed["anthropic_version"] == _VERTEX_ANTHROPIC_VERSION

71	def _strip_function_call_ids(gemini_payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
72	    """Remove ``id`` from functionCall/functionResponse parts of a Gemini request body.
73	
74	    The shared GeminiAdapter targets the Developer Gemini API
75	    (generativelanguage.googleapis.com), which uses ``functionCall``/``functionResponse``
76	    ``id`` to correlate parallel tool calls. Vertex AI's generateContent proto rejects
77	    that field with ``400 INVALID_ARGUMENT`` at ``contents[].parts[].function_call.id``,
78	    so strip it while leaving ``name`` and ``thoughtSignature`` intact. Mutates and
79	    returns ``gemini_payload``.
80	    """
81	    for content in gemini_payload.get("contents") or []:
82	        for part in content.get("parts") or []:
83	            if function_call := part.get("functionCall"):
84	                function_call.pop("id", None)
85	            if function_response := part.get("functionResponse"):
86	                function_response.pop("id", None)
87	    return gemini_payload

92	    filtered = {}
93	    for name, value in headers.items():
94	        if name.lower() != "anthropic-beta":
95	            filtered[name] = value
96	            continue
97	        if kept := [beta for beta in map(str.strip, value.split(",")) if beta in allowed]:
98	            filtered[name] = ",".join(kept)
99	    return filtered

98	def _parse_model_uri(model_uri: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
99	    """Parse a model URI of the form "<provider>:/<model-name>"."""
100	    # urllib.parse.urlparse is not used because provider names with underscores
101	    # (e.g., vertex_ai) are invalid in RFC 3986 URI schemes and would fail parsing.
102	    match model_uri.split(":/", 1):
103	        case [provider, model_path] if provider and model_path.lstrip("/"):
104	            return provider, model_path.lstrip("/")
105	        case _:
106	            raise MlflowException(
107	                f"Malformed model uri '{model_uri}'. The URI must be in the format of "
108	                "<provider>:/<model-name>, e.g., 'openai:/gpt-4.1-mini'.",
109	                error_code=INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
110	            )

113	def convert_mlflow_uri_to_litellm(model_uri: str) -> str:
114	    """
115	    Convert MLflow model URI format to LiteLLM format.
116	
117	    MLflow uses URIs like 'openai:/gpt-4' while LiteLLM expects 'openai/gpt-4'.
118	    For Databricks endpoints, MLflow uses 'endpoints:/endpoint-name' which needs
119	    to be converted to 'databricks/endpoints/endpoint-name' for LiteLLM.
120	
121	    Args:
122	        model_uri: MLflow model URI (e.g., 'openai:/gpt-4', 'endpoints:/my-endpoint')
123	
124	    Returns:
125	        LiteLLM-compatible model string (e.g., 'openai/gpt-4', 'databricks/endpoints/my-endpoint')
126	    """
127	    try:
128	        scheme, path = _parse_model_uri(model_uri)
129	    except Exception as e:
130	        raise MlflowException(f"Failed to convert MLflow model URI to LiteLLM format: {e}")
131	    if scheme in ("endpoints", "databricks"):
132	        return f"databricks/{path}"
133	    return f"{scheme}/{path}"

153	def _is_unsupported_output_format_error(exc: MlflowException) -> bool:
154	    """Check if the error indicates the model doesn't support structured output.
155	
156	    Older Anthropic models (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-20250514) don't support ``output_config``
157	    and return a 400 with::
158	
159	        {
160	            "type": "error",
161	            "error": {
162	                "type": "invalid_request_error",
163	                "message": "'claude-sonnet-4-20250514' does not support output format.",
164	            },
165	        }
166	
167	    Newer models (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) support it.
168	    """
169	    match exc.__cause__:
170	        case requests.exceptions.HTTPError(
171	            response=requests.Response(status_code=400) as response,
172	        ):
173	            try:
174	                body = response.json()
175	            except Exception:
176	                return False
177	            match body:
178	                case {
179	                    "error": {
180	                        "type": "invalid_request_error",
181	                        "message": str(msg),
182	                    }
183	                }:
184	                    return "does not support output format" in msg.lower()
185	    return False

188	def _call_llm_provider_api(
189	    provider_name: str,
190	    model: str,
191	    input_data: str | None = None,
192	    eval_parameters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
193	    extra_headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
194	    proxy_url: str | None = None,
195	    *,
196	    messages: list[dict[str, str]] | None = None,
197	    response_format: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
198	) -> str:
199	    """
200	    Invoke chat endpoint of various LLM providers.
201	
202	    Under the hood, this function uses the MLflow Gateway to transform the input/output data
203	    for different LLM providers.
204	
205	    Args:
206	        provider_name: The provider name, e.g., "anthropic".
207	        model: The model name, e.g., "claude-3-5-sonnet"
208	        input_data: The input string prompt to send to the model as a chat message.
209	            Mutually exclusive with ``messages``.
210	        eval_parameters: The additional parameters to send to the model, e.g. temperature.
211	        extra_headers: The additional headers to send to the provider.
212	        proxy_url: Proxy URL to be used for the judge model. If not specified, the default
213	            URL for the LLM provider will be used.
214	        messages: Pre-built list of message dicts (``[{"role": ..., "content": ...}]``).
215	            Mutually exclusive with ``input_data``.
216	        response_format: Response format dict (e.g. from ``pydantic_to_response_format``).
217	    """
218	    from mlflow.gateway.config import Provider
219	    from mlflow.gateway.schemas import chat
220	
221	    if (input_data is None) == (messages is None):
222	        raise MlflowException.invalid_parameter_value(
223	            "Exactly one of input_data or messages must be provided."
224	        )
225	
226	    eval_parameters = eval_parameters or {}
227	    extra_headers = extra_headers or {}
228	    provider = _get_provider_instance(provider_name, model, base_url=proxy_url)
229	
230	    if messages is not None:
231	        payload = {"messages": messages} | eval_parameters
232	        if response_format is not None:
233	            payload["response_format"] = response_format
234	    else:
235	        chat_request = chat.RequestPayload(
236	            model=model,
237	            messages=[
238	                chat.RequestMessage(role="user", content=input_data),
239	            ],
240	            **eval_parameters,
241	        )
242	
243	        # Filter out keys in the payload to the specified ones + "messages".
244	        # Does not include "model" key here because some providers do not accept it as a
245	        # part of the payload. Whether or not to include "model" key must be determined
246	        # by each provider implementation.
247	        filtered_keys = {"messages", *eval_parameters.keys()}
248	
249	        payload = {
250	            k: v
251	            for k, v in chat_request.model_dump(exclude_none=True).items()
252	            if (v is not None) and (k in filtered_keys)
253	        }
254	
255	    chat_payload = provider.adapter_class.chat_to_model(payload, provider.config)
256	    if messages is None:
257	        # eval_parameters were filtered out by the RequestPayload serialization;
258	        # re-apply them. When messages is not None, they're already in the payload.
259	        chat_payload.update(eval_parameters)
260	
261	    if normalize_provider_name(provider_name) == Provider.BEDROCK:
262	        if proxy_url or extra_headers:
263	            _logger.warning(
264	                "Proxy URL and extra headers are not supported for Bedrock LLMs. "
265	                "Ignoring the provided proxy URL and extra headers.",
266	            )
267	        response = provider._request(chat_payload)
268	    else:
269	        if (provider_name, model) in _MODELS_WITHOUT_OUTPUT_CONFIG:
270	            chat_payload.pop("output_config", None)
271	            chat_payload.pop("response_format", None)
272	
273	        try:
274	            response = _send_request(
275	                endpoint=proxy_url or provider.get_endpoint_url("llm/v1/chat"),
276	                headers=provider.headers | extra_headers,
277	                payload=chat_payload,
278	            )
279	        except MlflowException as e:
280	            if provider_name != "anthropic" or not _is_unsupported_output_format_error(e):
281	                raise
282	            # Model doesn't support structured output; remember and retry.
283	            _MODELS_WITHOUT_OUTPUT_CONFIG.add((provider_name, model))
284	            chat_payload.pop("output_config", None)
285	            chat_payload.pop("response_format", None)
286	            response = _send_request(
287	                endpoint=proxy_url or provider.get_endpoint_url("llm/v1/chat"),
288	                headers=provider.headers | extra_headers,
289	                payload=chat_payload,
290	            )
291	    chat_response = provider.adapter_class.model_to_chat(response, provider.config)
292	    if len(chat_response.choices) == 0:
293	        raise MlflowException(
294	            "Failed to score the provided input as the judge LLM did not return "
295	            "any chat completion results in the response."
296	        )
297	    content = chat_response.choices[0].message.content
298	
299	    # NB: Evaluation only handles text content for now.
300	    return content[0].text if isinstance(content, list) else content

550	def call_deployments_api(

554	    endpoint_type: str | None = None,
555	):
556	    """Call the deployment endpoint with the given payload and parameters.
557	
558	    Args:
559	        deployment_uri: The URI of the deployment endpoint.
560	        input_data: The input string or dictionary to send to the endpoint.
561	            - If it is a string, MLflow tries to construct the payload based on the endpoint type.
562	            - If it is a dictionary, MLflow directly sends it to the endpoint.
563	        eval_parameters: The evaluation parameters to send to the endpoint.
564	        endpoint_type: The type of the endpoint. If specified, must be 'llm/v1/completions'
565	            or 'llm/v1/chat'. If not specified, MLflow tries to get the endpoint type
566	            from the endpoint, and if not found, directly sends the payload to the endpoint.
567	
568	    Returns:
569	        The unpacked response from the endpoint.
570	    """
571	    from mlflow.deployments import get_deploy_client
572	
573	    client = get_deploy_client()
574

576	        payload = _construct_payload_from_str(input_data, endpoint_type)
577	    elif isinstance(input_data, dict):
578	        # If the input is a dictionary, we assume it is already in the correct format
579	        payload = input_data
580	    else:

582	            f"Invalid input data type {type(input_data)}. Must be a string or a dictionary.",
583	            error_code=INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
584	        )
585	    payload = {**payload, **(eval_parameters or {})}
586	
587	    try:
588	        response = client.predict(endpoint=deployment_uri, inputs=payload)
589	    except Exception as e:
590	        raise MlflowException(
591	            _PREDICT_ERROR_MSG.format(e=e, uri=deployment_uri, payload=payload)
592	        ) from e

597	def _construct_payload_from_str(prompt: str, endpoint_type: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
598	    """
599	    Construct the payload from the input string based on the endpoint type.
600	    If the endpoint type is not specified or unsupported one, raise an exception.
601	    """
602	    if endpoint_type == "llm/v1/completions":
603	        return {"prompt": prompt}
604	    elif endpoint_type == "llm/v1/chat":
605	        return {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]}
606	    else:
607	        raise MlflowException(
608	            f"Unsupported endpoint type: {endpoint_type}. If string input is provided, "
609	            "the endpoint type must be 'llm/v1/completions' or 'llm/v1/chat'.",
610	            error_code=INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
611	        )

614	def _parse_response(
615	    response: dict[str, Any], endpoint_type: str | None
616	) -> str | None | dict[str, Any]:
617	    if endpoint_type == "llm/v1/completions":
618	        return _parse_completions_response_format(response)

49	class _TokenCounter:
50	    """Thread-safe accumulator for LLM token usage across pipeline phases."""
51	
52	    def __init__(
53	        self,
54	        model: str,
55	        input_tokens: int = 0,
56	        output_tokens: int = 0,
57	        cost_usd: float = 0.0,
58	    ):
59	        self._lock = threading.RLock()
60	        self.input_tokens = input_tokens
61	        self.output_tokens = output_tokens
62	        self._cost_usd = cost_usd
63	        self._cost_resolved = False
64	        provider, model_name = _parse_model_uri(model)
65	        if provider == "gateway":
66	            self._model = _resolve_model_for_gateway(model_name)
67	        else:
68	            self._model = model
69	
70	    @property
71	    def cost_usd(self) -> float | None:
72	        """Return the total cost, falling back to the LiteLLM pricing API if needed."""
73	        with self._lock:
74	            if self._cost_usd == 0 and not self._cost_resolved:
75	                total = self.input_tokens + self.output_tokens
76	                if total > 0 and self._model:
77	                    if cost := _lookup_model_cost(
78	                        self._model, self.input_tokens, self.output_tokens
79	                    ):
80	                        self._cost_usd = cost
81	                # Mark resolved once we've attempted lookup with tokens present,
82	                # or when there are no tokens yet (nothing to look up).
83	                self._cost_resolved = total > 0 or not self._model
84	            return self._cost_usd or None
85	
86	    def add_cost(self, cost: float) -> None:
87	        with self._lock:
88	            self._cost_usd += cost
89	
90	    def track(self, response: litellm.ModelResponse | ResponsePayload) -> None:
91	        with self._lock:
92	            if response.usage:
93	                self.input_tokens += response.usage.prompt_tokens or 0
94	                self.output_tokens += response.usage.completion_tokens or 0
95	            if hidden := getattr(response, "_hidden_params", None):
96	                if cost := hidden.get("response_cost"):
97	                    self.add_cost(cost)
98	
99	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, int | float]:
100	        result = {}
101	        total = self.input_tokens + self.output_tokens
102	        if total > 0:
103	            result["input_tokens"] = self.input_tokens
104	            result["output_tokens"] = self.output_tokens
105	            result["total_tokens"] = total
106	        if cost := self.cost_usd:
107	            result["cost_usd"] = round(cost, 6)

196	def _call_llm_via_gateway(
197	    model: str,
198	    messages: list[dict[str, str]],
199	    *,
200	    json_mode: bool = False,
201	    response_format: type[pydantic.BaseModel] | None = None,
202	    token_counter: _TokenCounter | None = None,
203	    inference_params: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
204	    max_tokens: int = _DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS,
205	    num_retries: int = _DEFAULT_NUM_RETRIES,
206	) -> Any:
207	    # Lightweight fallback for when LiteLLM is not installed. Supports
208	    # providers with MLflow gateway adapters (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Mistral)
209	    # and the MLflow AI Gateway (gateway:/ URIs).
210	    # Known gaps vs the LiteLLM path: no drop_params
211	    # (https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/completion/drop_params) - LiteLLM silently
212	    # strips unsupported params (e.g. response_format) per model before sending
213	    # the request, while this path sends them as-is. Not an issue for OpenAI
214	    # and Anthropic which both support structured outputs. Also missing:
215	    # no context window management and no per-request cost tracking.
216	    provider_name, model_name = _parse_model_uri(model)
217	    provider = _get_provider_instance(provider_name, model_name)
218	
219	    payload = {"messages": messages, "max_completion_tokens": max_tokens}
220	    if inference_params:
221	        payload.update(inference_params)
222	    if response_format is not None:
223	        payload["response_format"] = pydantic_to_response_format(response_format)
224	    elif json_mode:
225	        payload["response_format"] = {"type": "json_object"}
226	
227	    chat_payload = provider.adapter_class.chat_to_model(payload, provider.config)
228	
229	    for attempt in range(num_retries + 1):
230	        try:
231	            raw_response = _send_request(
232	                endpoint=provider.get_endpoint_url(EndpointType.LLM_V1_CHAT),
233	                headers=provider.headers,
234	                payload=chat_payload,
235	            )
236	            break
237	        except (
238	            requests.exceptions.RequestException,
239	            mlflow.exceptions.MlflowException,
240	        ):
241	            if attempt >= num_retries:
242	                raise
243	            time.sleep(2**attempt)
244	
245	    response = provider.adapter_class.model_to_chat(raw_response, provider.config)
246	    if token_counter is not None:
247	        token_counter.track(response)
248	    return response

276	        return input_tokens * cost.input_cost_per_token + output_tokens * cost.output_cost_per_token

200	    Uses the provider's adapter to transform the raw response into a
201	    normalized format, then extracts the assistant message and usage metadata.
202	
203	    Returns:
204	        Tuple of (ChatMessage, usage_dict) where usage_dict has
205	        "prompt_tokens" and "completion_tokens" keys.
206	    """
207	    # Lazy import: mlflow.types.llm → mlflow.types.schema → numpy, which breaks
208	    # the skinny client. Must stay inside the function.
209	    from mlflow.types.llm import ChatMessage
210	
211	    chat_response = provider.adapter_class.model_to_chat(response_data, provider.config)
212	    if not chat_response.choices:
213	        raise MlflowException("Empty choices in chat completions response")
214	
215	    resp_msg = chat_response.choices[0].message
216	    content = resp_msg.content
217	    # Flatten list content (e.g. Anthropic text blocks) to string
218	    if isinstance(content, list):
219	        content = "\n".join(part.text for part in content if hasattr(part, "text") and part.text)
220	        content = content or None
221	
222	    tool_calls_raw = None
223	    if resp_msg.tool_calls:
224	        # Convert gateway ToolCall objects back to dicts for ChatMessage auto-conversion
225	        tool_calls_raw = [
226	            {
227	                "id": tc.id,
228	                "type": getattr(tc, "type", "function"),
229	                "function": {
230	                    "name": tc.function.name,
231	                    "arguments": tc.function.arguments,
232	                },
233	            }
234	            for tc in resp_msg.tool_calls
235	        ]
236	
237	    # ChatMessage requires content when tool_calls is absent
238	    if content is None and not tool_calls_raw:
239	        content = ""
240	
241	    usage = {}
242	    if chat_response.usage:
243	        usage = {
244	            "prompt_tokens": getattr(chat_response.usage, "prompt_tokens", None),
245	            "completion_tokens": getattr(chat_response.usage, "completion_tokens", None),
246	        }
247	
248	    return (
249	        ChatMessage(
250	            role=resp_msg.role,
251	            content=content,
252	            tool_calls=tool_calls_raw,
253	        ),
254	        usage,
255	    )

259	# Single-shot gateway invocation (no tool calling)
260	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

262	
263	def _invoke_via_gateway(
264	    model_uri: str,
265	    provider: str,
266	    prompt: str | list[dict[str, str]],
267	    inference_params: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
268	    response_format: type[pydantic.BaseModel] | None = None,
269	    base_url: str | None = None,
270	    extra_headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
271	) -> str:
272	    """
273	    Invoke the judge model via native AI Gateway adapters.
274	
275	    Supports both string prompts (via ``score_model_on_payload``) and
276	    ChatMessage-style message lists (via the provider infrastructure).
277	
278	    Args:
279	        model_uri: The full model URI.
280	        provider: The provider name.
281	        prompt: The prompt to evaluate. Either a string or a list of message dicts.
282	        inference_params: Optional dictionary of inference parameters to pass to the
283	            model (e.g., temperature, top_p, max_tokens).
284	        response_format: Optional Pydantic model class for structured output.
285	            Only used for ChatMessage-style prompts.
286	        base_url: Optional base URL to route requests through.
287	        extra_headers: Optional extra HTTP headers.
288	
289	    Returns:
290	        The JSON response string from the model.
291	
292	    Raises:
293	        MlflowException: If the provider is not supported or invocation fails.
294	    """
295	    if provider == "gateway":
296	        workspace_headers: dict[str, str] = {}
297	        if ws := get_request_workspace():
298	            workspace_headers[WORKSPACE_HEADER_NAME] = ws
299	        extra_headers = {**workspace_headers, **(extra_headers or {})}
300	
301	    if isinstance(prompt, str):
302	        return score_model_on_payload(
303	            model_uri=model_uri,
304	            payload=prompt,
305	            eval_parameters=inference_params,
306	            extra_headers=extra_headers,
307	            proxy_url=base_url,
308	            endpoint_type=get_endpoint_type(model_uri) or EndpointType.LLM_V1_CHAT,
309	        )
310	
311	    _, model_name = _parse_model_uri(model_uri)
312	    rf_dict = pydantic_to_response_format(response_format) if response_format else None
313	    return _call_llm_provider_api(
314	        provider,
315	        model_name,
316	        messages=prompt,
317	        eval_parameters=inference_params,
318	        extra_headers=extra_headers,
319	        proxy_url=base_url,
320	        response_format=rf_dict,
321	    )

326	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

328	
329	class GatewayAdapter(BaseJudgeAdapter):
330	    """Adapter for native AI Gateway providers."""
331	
332	    @classmethod
333	    def is_applicable(
334	        cls,
335	        model_uri: str,
336	        prompt: str | list["ChatMessage"],
337	    ) -> bool:
338	        model_provider, _ = _parse_model_uri(model_uri)
339	        if not is_supported_provider(model_provider) and model_provider not in {
340	            "endpoints",
341	            "gateway",
342	        }:
343	            return False
344	        # "endpoints" (Databricks model serving) only supports string prompts
345	        # via score_model_on_payload; _get_provider_instance doesn't handle it.
346	        if isinstance(prompt, list) and model_provider == "endpoints":
347	            return False
348	        return True
349	
350	    def _invoke(self, input_params: AdapterInvocationInput) -> AdapterInvocationOutput:
351	        # base_url and extra_headers are not supported for deployment endpoints
352	        if input_params.model_provider == "endpoints" and (
353	            input_params.base_url is not None or input_params.extra_headers is not None
354	        ):
355	            raise MlflowException(
356	                "base_url and extra_headers are not supported for deployment "
357	                "endpoints (endpoints:/...). The endpoint URL is determined by the "
358	                "deployment target configuration.",
359	                error_code=INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
360	            )
361	
362	        # For all providers except "endpoints", always use the tool-calling loop —
363	        # even when trace=None (no tools). _invoke_with_tools extracts token usage
364	        # from the API response which enables JUDGE_COST tracking.
365	        # "endpoints" (Databricks model serving) uses score_model_on_payload and
366	        # does not support the provider-based request/response transformation.
367	        if input_params.model_provider != "endpoints":
368	            return self._invoke_with_tools(input_params)
369	
370	        # "endpoints" provider: trace-based tool calling is not supported.
371	        if input_params.trace is not None:
372	            raise MlflowException(
373	                "Trace-based tool calling is not supported for deployment endpoints "
374	                "(endpoints:/...). Use a direct provider URI (e.g. openai:/gpt-4) instead.",
375	                error_code=BAD_REQUEST,
376	            )
377	
378	        if isinstance(input_params.prompt, str):
379	            prompt = input_params.prompt
380	        else:
381	            prompt = [{"role": msg.role, "content": msg.content} for msg in input_params.prompt]
382	
383	        response = _invoke_via_gateway(
384	            input_params.model_uri,
385	            input_params.model_provider,
386	            prompt,
387	            inference_params=input_params.inference_params,
388	            response_format=input_params.response_format,
389	            base_url=input_params.base_url,
390	            extra_headers=input_params.extra_headers,
391	        )
392	
393	        cleaned_response = _strip_markdown_code_blocks(response)
394	
395	        try:
396	            response_dict = json.loads(cleaned_response, strict=False)
397	        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
398	            raise MlflowException(
399	                f"Failed to parse response from judge model. Response: {response}",
400	                error_code=BAD_REQUEST,
401	            ) from e
402	
403	        feedback = Feedback(
404	            name=input_params.assessment_name,
405	            value=response_dict["result"],
406	            rationale=_sanitize_justification(response_dict.get("rationale", "")),
407	            source=AssessmentSource(
408	                source_type=AssessmentSourceType.LLM_JUDGE, source_id=input_params.model_uri
409	            ),
410	        )
411	
412	        return AdapterInvocationOutput(feedback=feedback)
413	
414	    def invoke_with_structured_output(
415	        self,
416	        model_uri: str,
417	        messages: list["ChatMessage"],
418	        output_schema: type[pydantic.BaseModel],
419	        trace: "Trace | None" = None,
420	        num_retries: int = 10,
421	        inference_params: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
422	    ) -> pydantic.BaseModel:
423	        """Invoke the model and parse the response into a Pydantic schema."""
424	        provider, model_name = _parse_model_uri(model_uri)
425	
426	        output = self._invoke_and_handle_tools(
427	            provider=provider,
428	            model_name=model_name,
429	            messages=messages,
430	            trace=trace,
431	            num_retries=num_retries,
432	            response_format=output_schema,
433	            inference_params=inference_params,
434	        )
435	
436	        cleaned_response = _strip_markdown_code_blocks(output.response)
437	        try:
438	            response_dict = json.loads(cleaned_response, strict=False)
439	        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
440	            raise MlflowException(
441	                f"Failed to parse response from judge model. Response: {output.response}",
442	                error_code=BAD_REQUEST,
443	            ) from e
444	        return output_schema(**response_dict)
445	
446	    def _invoke_with_tools(self, input_params: AdapterInvocationInput) -> AdapterInvocationOutput:
447	        """Invoke the judge model with trace-based tool calling support."""
448	        # Lazy import: mlflow.types.llm pulls in numpy via mlflow.types.schema
449	        from mlflow.types.llm import ChatMessage
450	
451	        messages = (
452	            [ChatMessage(role="user", content=input_params.prompt)]
453	            if isinstance(input_params.prompt, str)
454	            else input_params.prompt
455	        )
456	
457	        output = self._invoke_and_handle_tools(
458	            provider=input_params.model_provider,
459	            model_name=input_params.model_name,
460	            messages=messages,
461	            trace=input_params.trace,
462	            num_retries=input_params.num_retries,
463	            response_format=input_params.response_format,
464	            inference_params=input_params.inference_params,
465	            base_url=input_params.base_url,
466	            extra_headers=input_params.extra_headers,
467	        )
468	
469	        cleaned_response = _strip_markdown_code_blocks(output.response)
470	
471	        try:
472	            response_dict = json.loads(cleaned_response, strict=False)
473	        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
474	            raise MlflowException(
475	                f"Failed to parse response from judge model. Response: {output.response}",
476	                error_code=BAD_REQUEST,
477	            ) from e
478	
479	        cost = None
480	        if output.num_prompt_tokens is not None and output.num_completion_tokens is not None:
481	            cost = _lookup_model_cost(
482	                input_params.model_uri,
483	                output.num_prompt_tokens,
484	                output.num_completion_tokens,
485	            )
486	
487	        metadata = {}
488	        if cost is not None:
489	            metadata[AssessmentMetadataKey.JUDGE_COST] = cost
490	        if output.num_prompt_tokens is not None:
491	            metadata[AssessmentMetadataKey.JUDGE_INPUT_TOKENS] = output.num_prompt_tokens
492	        if output.num_completion_tokens is not None:
493	            metadata[AssessmentMetadataKey.JUDGE_OUTPUT_TOKENS] = output.num_completion_tokens
494	        metadata = metadata or None
495	
496	        feedback = Feedback(
497	            name=input_params.assessment_name,
498	            value=response_dict["result"],
499	            rationale=_sanitize_justification(response_dict.get("rationale", "")),
500	            source=AssessmentSource(
501	                source_type=AssessmentSourceType.LLM_JUDGE, source_id=input_params.model_uri
502	            ),
503	            trace_id=input_params.trace.info.trace_id if input_params.trace else None,
504	            metadata=metadata,
505	        )
506	
507	        return AdapterInvocationOutput(
508	            feedback=feedback,
509	            request_id=output.request_id,
510	            num_prompt_tokens=output.num_prompt_tokens,
511	            num_completion_tokens=output.num_completion_tokens,
512	            cost=cost,
513	        )
514	
515	    # TODO: Consider extending _call_llm_provider_api to accept `tools` and return
516	    # the full ChatResponse (not just text). This would allow replacing the custom
517	    # send_chat_request + provider adapter calls below with a single shared util.
518	    def _invoke_and_handle_tools(
519	        self,
520	        provider: str,
521	        model_name: str,
522	        messages: list["ChatMessage"],
523	        trace: "Trace | None",
524	        num_retries: int,
525	        response_format: type[pydantic.BaseModel] | None = None,
526	        inference_params: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
527	        base_url: str | None = None,
528	        extra_headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
529	    ) -> InvokeOutput:
530	        """Run the tool-calling loop using the provider infrastructure for HTTP calls."""
531	        # Lazy import: mlflow.types.llm pulls in numpy via mlflow.types.schema
532	        from mlflow.types.llm import ChatMessage
533	
534	        # Resolve provider for config, URL, headers, and request/response transformation.
535	        # Each provider's get_endpoint_url() returns the full endpoint path
536	        # (e.g. OpenAI: .../chat/completions, Anthropic: .../messages).
537	        provider_instance = _get_provider_instance(provider, model_name, base_url=base_url)
538	        endpoint = base_url or provider_instance.get_endpoint_url("llm/v1/chat")
539	        headers = dict(provider_instance.headers or {})
540	        # Tag gateway requests so the server can attribute traffic to the judge
541	        if provider == "gateway":
542	            headers[MLFLOW_GATEWAY_CALLER_HEADER] = GatewayCaller.JUDGE.value
543	            if ws := get_request_workspace():
544	                headers[WORKSPACE_HEADER_NAME] = ws
545	        if extra_headers:
546	            headers.update(extra_headers)
547	
548	        judge_messages = [ChatMessage(role=msg.role, content=msg.content) for msg in messages]
549	
550	        tools = []
551	        if trace is not None:
552	            judge_tools = list_judge_tools()
553	            tools = [tool.get_definition().to_dict() for tool in judge_tools]
554	
555	        include_response_format = _MODEL_RESPONSE_FORMAT_CAPABILITIES.get(
556	            f"{provider}/{model_name}", True
557	        )
558	
559	        max_context_tokens = _get_max_context_tokens(provider, model_name)
560	        max_iterations = MLFLOW_JUDGE_MAX_ITERATIONS.get()
561	        iteration_count = 0
562	        total_prompt_tokens: int | None = None
563	        total_completion_tokens: int | None = None
564	
565	        while True:
566	            iteration_count += 1
567	            if iteration_count > max_iterations:
568	                _raise_iteration_limit_exceeded(max_iterations)
569	
570	            try:
571	                payload = _build_request(
572	                    messages=judge_messages,
573	                    tools=tools or None,
574	                    response_format=response_format,
575	                    include_response_format=include_response_format,
576	                    inference_params=inference_params,
577	                )
578	
579	                # Use the provider adapter to transform the request
580	                # (e.g. adds model name, converts tool format for Anthropic)
581	                chat_payload = provider_instance.adapter_class.chat_to_model(
582	                    payload, provider_instance.config
583	                )
584	
585	                try:
586	                    response_data = send_chat_request(
587	                        endpoint=endpoint,
588	                        headers=headers,
589	                        payload=chat_payload,
590	                        num_retries=num_retries,
591	                    )
592	                except ChatCompletionError as e:
593	                    if e.is_context_window_error:
594	                        pruned = _remove_oldest_tool_call_pair(judge_messages)
595	                        if pruned is None:
596	                            raise MlflowException(
597	                                "Context window exceeded and there are no tool calls to "
598	                                "truncate. The initial prompt may be too long for the "
599	                                "model's context window."
600	                            ) from e
601	                        judge_messages = pruned
602	                        continue
603	
604	                    if (
605	                        e.status_code == 400
606	                        and include_response_format
607	                        and is_response_format_error(e.message)
608	                    ):
609	                        _logger.debug(
610	                            f"Model {provider}/{model_name} may not support structured "
611	                            f"outputs. Error: {e.message}. Falling back to unstructured "
612	                            f"response.",
613	                        )
614	                        _MODEL_RESPONSE_FORMAT_CAPABILITIES[f"{provider}/{model_name}"] = False
615	                        include_response_format = False
616	                        continue
617	
618	                    # Map HTTP status codes to appropriate MLflow error codes
619	                    if e.status_code == 400:
620	                        error_code = BAD_REQUEST
621	                    elif e.status_code in (401, 403):
622	                        error_code = INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE
623	                    else:
624	                        error_code = INTERNAL_ERROR
625	
626	                    raise MlflowException(
627	                        f"Failed to invoke judge model: {e.message}",
628	                        error_code=error_code,
629	                    ) from e
630	
631	                # Use the provider adapter to normalize the response
632	                message, usage = _parse_response_message(response_data, provider_instance)
633	
634	                if (prompt_tokens := usage.get("prompt_tokens")) is not None:
635	                    total_prompt_tokens = (total_prompt_tokens or 0) + prompt_tokens
636	                if (completion_tokens := usage.get("completion_tokens")) is not None:
637	                    total_completion_tokens = (total_completion_tokens or 0) + completion_tokens
638	
639	                if not message.tool_calls:
640	                    return InvokeOutput(
641	                        response=message.content,
642	                        request_id=response_data.get("id"),
643	                        num_prompt_tokens=total_prompt_tokens,
644	                        num_completion_tokens=total_completion_tokens,
645	                    )
646	
647	                judge_messages.append(message)
648	                tool_response_messages = _process_tool_calls(
649	                    tool_calls=message.tool_calls, trace=trace
650	                )
651	                judge_messages.extend(tool_response_messages)
652	
653	                # Proactively prune if approaching context window limit,
654	                # using the actual prompt_tokens from the LLM response.
655	                if _should_proactively_prune(usage, max_context_tokens):
656	                    pruned = _remove_oldest_tool_call_pair(judge_messages)
657	                    if pruned is not None:
658	                        _logger.debug(
659	                            f"Proactively pruned conversation history "
660	                            f"(prompt_tokens={usage.get('prompt_tokens')}, "
661	                            f"max={max_context_tokens})"
662	                        )
663	                        judge_messages = pruned
664	
665	            except MlflowException:
666	                raise
667	            except Exception as e:
668	                raise MlflowException(
669	                    f"Failed to invoke the judge model: {e}",
670	                    error_code=INTERNAL_ERROR,
671	                ) from e

152	class _FailingResponse:
153	    """Response double for an upstream error, with the body shapes set per test.
154	
155	    ``json``/``text`` raise for ``_UNREADABLE``, standing in for a response that is not
156	    JSON, or whose body cannot be read at all. aiohttp's own ``json()`` returns None for
157	    an empty body and its ``text()`` returns "", which tests pass explicitly.
158	    """

160	    def __init__(
161	        self, json_body=_UNREADABLE, text_body=_UNREADABLE, status=400, message="Bad Request"
162	    ):
163	        self.status = status
164	        self.message = message
165	        self._json_body = json_body
166	        self._text_body = text_body
167	
168	    def raise_for_status(self):
169	        raise aiohttp.ClientResponseError(None, None, status=self.status, message=self.message)
170	
171	    async def json(self):
172	        if self._json_body is _UNREADABLE:
173	            raise ValueError("body is not JSON")
174	        return self._json_body
175	
176	    async def text(self):
177	        if self._text_body is _UNREADABLE:
178	            raise ValueError("body could not be read")
179	        return self._text_body

974	def _event_stream_message(headers: dict[str, str], payload: bytes) -> bytes:
975	    # AWS event stream framing: a prelude (total length, headers length, prelude CRC),
976	    # string-valued headers, the payload, then a CRC over the whole message.
977	    encoded_headers = b"".join(
978	        bytes([len(name)])
979	        + name.encode()
980	        + b"\x07"
981	        + struct.pack(">H", len(value))
982	        + value.encode()
983	        for name, value in headers.items()
984	    )
985	    prelude = struct.pack(">II", 16 + len(encoded_headers) + len(payload), len(encoded_headers))
986	    message = prelude + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(prelude)) + encoded_headers + payload
987	    return message + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(message))

990	def _bedrock_chunk(event: dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
991	    return _event_stream_message(
992	        {":event-type": "chunk", ":content-type": "application/json", ":message-type": "event"},
993	        json.dumps({"bytes": base64.b64encode(json.dumps(event).encode()).decode()}).encode(),
994	    )

blobs.5f19fcc96890:
1	---
2	title: Model Providers
3	description: Supported LLM providers in MLflow AI Gateway including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, and Vertex AI. Configure endpoints and use passthrough APIs.
4	---
5	
6	import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
7	import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";
8	
9	# Model Providers
10	
11	MLflow AI Gateway supports many model providers natively, without requiring any additional dependencies. For providers not listed here, you can optionally install [LiteLLM](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers) to extend the gateway to use them. LiteLLM is not a dependency of MLflow AI Gateway—it is only used if you choose to install it in your environment. This page covers the major providers, their capabilities, and how to use their passthrough APIs.
12	
13	## Supported Providers
14	
15	The AI Gateway supports providers across these categories:
16	
17	### Major Cloud Providers
18	
19	| Provider          | Chat | Embeddings | Passthrough API                                    |
20	| ----------------- | ---- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
21	| **OpenAI**        | Yes  | Yes        | `/gateway/openai/v1/...`                           |
22	| **Anthropic**     | Yes  | No         | `/gateway/anthropic/v1/...`                        |
23	| **Google Gemini** | Yes  | Yes        | `/gateway/gemini/v1beta/...`                       |
24	| **Azure OpenAI**  | Yes  | Yes        | Via OpenAI passthrough                             |
25	| **AWS Bedrock**   | Yes  | Yes        | Anthropic passthrough (Claude, API key auth)       |
26	| **Vertex AI**     | Yes  | Yes        | Anthropic, Gemini, or OpenAI passthrough, by model |
27	
28	### Additional Providers
29	
30	| Provider         | Chat | Embeddings | Notes                                |
31	| ---------------- | ---- | ---------- | ------------------------------------ |
32	| **Cohere**       | Yes  | Yes        | Command and Embed models             |
33	| **Mistral**      | Yes  | Yes        | Mistral AI models                    |
34	| **Groq**         | Yes  | No         | Open-source models                   |
35	| **Together AI**  | Yes  | Yes        | Open-source models                   |
36	| **Fireworks AI** | Yes  | Yes        | Open-source models                   |
37	| **Ollama**       | Yes  | Yes        | Local models                         |
38	| **Databricks**   | Yes  | Yes        | Foundation Model APIs                |
39	| **Portkey**      | Yes  | Yes        | Unified gateway for any LLM provider |
40	
41	For a complete list of supported providers, view the provider dropdown when creating an endpoint or see the [LiteLLM documentation](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers).
42	
43	### Evaluation Providers
44	
45	| Provider     | Model family | Passthrough API                  |
46	| ------------ | ------------ | -------------------------------- |
47	| **TypeSafe** | Jev          | `/gateway/typesafe/v1/systemone` |
48	
49	TypeSafe endpoints support structured System One evaluation requests. They do not support the gateway's chat, embeddings, OpenAI-compatible, or streaming APIs.
50	
51	## Provider-Specific Passthrough APIs
52	
53	### OpenAI
54	
55	The OpenAI passthrough exposes the full OpenAI API:
56	
57	**Base URL:** `http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1`
58	
59	**Supported Endpoints:**
60	
61	- `POST /chat/completions` - Chat completions
62	- `POST /embeddings` - Text embeddings
63	- `POST /responses` - Responses API (multi-turn conversations)
64	
65	<Tabs>
66	<TabItem value="python" label="Python SDK" default>
67	
68	```python
69	from openai import OpenAI
70	
71	client = OpenAI(
72	    base_url="http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1",
73	    api_key="dummy",  # Not needed, configured server-side
74	)
75	
76	# Chat completion
77	response = client.chat.completions.create(
78	    model="my-endpoint",
79	    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
80	)
81	
82	# Embeddings
83	embeddings = client.embeddings.create(
84	    model="my-embeddings-endpoint",
85	    input="Text to embed",
86	)
87	
88	# Responses API
89	response = client.responses.create(
90	    model="my-endpoint",
91	    input="Hello!",
92	)
93	```
94	
95	</TabItem>
96	<TabItem value="curl" label="cURL">
97	
98	```bash
99	# Chat completion
100	curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1/chat/completions \
101	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
102	  -d '{"model": "my-endpoint", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]}'
103	
104	# Embeddings
105	curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1/embeddings \
106	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
107	  -d '{"model": "my-embeddings-endpoint", "input": "Text to embed"}'
108	
109	# Responses API
110	curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1/responses \
111	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
112	  -d '{"model": "my-endpoint", "input": "Hello!"}'
113	```
114	
115	</TabItem>
116	</Tabs>
117	
118	See [OpenAI API Reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference) for complete documentation.
119	
120	### Anthropic
121	
122	Access Claude models through the Anthropic passthrough:
123	
124	**Base URL:** `http://localhost:5000/gateway/anthropic`
125	
126	**Supported Endpoints:**
127	
128	- `POST /v1/messages` - Messages API
129	
130	<Tabs>
131	<TabItem value="python" label="Python SDK" default>
132	
133	```python
134	import anthropic
135	
136	client = anthropic.Anthropic(
137	    base_url="http://localhost:5000/gateway/anthropic",
138	    api_key="dummy",  # Not needed, configured server-side
139	)
140	
141	response = client.messages.create(
142	    model="my-endpoint",
143	    max_tokens=1024,
144	    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
145	)
146	print(response.content[0].text)
147	```
148	
149	</TabItem>
150	<TabItem value="curl" label="cURL">
151	
152	```bash
153	curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/anthropic/v1/messages \
154	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
155	  -d '{
156	    "model": "my-endpoint",
157	    "max_tokens": 1024,
158	    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
159	  }'
160	```
161	
162	</TabItem>
163	</Tabs>
164	
165	See [Anthropic API Reference](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api) for complete documentation.
166	
167	### Google Gemini
168	
169	Access Gemini models through Google's API format:
170	
171	**Base URL:** `http://localhost:5000/gateway/gemini`
172	
173	**Supported Endpoints:**
174	
175	- `POST /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent` - Content generation
176	- `POST /v1beta/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent` - Streaming generation
177	
178	<Tabs>
179	<TabItem value="python" label="Python SDK" default>
180	
181	```python
182	from google import genai
183	
184	client = genai.Client(
185	    api_key="dummy",
186	    http_options={
187	        "base_url": "http://localhost:5000/gateway/gemini",
188	    },
189	)
190	
191	response = client.models.generate_content(
192	    model="my-endpoint",
193	    contents={"text": "Hello!"},
194	)
195	client.close()
196	print(response.candidates[0].content.parts[0].text)
197	```
198	
199	</TabItem>
200	<TabItem value="curl" label="cURL">
201	
202	```bash
203	curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/gemini/v1beta/models/my-endpoint:generateContent \
204	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
205	  -d '{"contents": [{"parts": [{"text": "Hello!"}]}]}'
206	```
207	
208	</TabItem>
209	</Tabs>
210	
211	See [Google Gemini API Reference](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs) for complete documentation.
212	
213	### Vertex AI
214	
215	Vertex AI endpoints use the passthrough API of the model family they serve: Claude models take the [Anthropic](#anthropic) routes, Gemini models take the [Google Gemini](#google-gemini) routes, and partner MaaS models (Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek, and others) take the [OpenAI](#openai) routes. Requests are authenticated server-side with the endpoint's Google Cloud credentials.
216	
217	Vertex AI validates the `anthropic-beta` header against the betas it supports, which lag behind the Anthropic API, and rejects the whole request when it sees a value it does not know. The `vertex_anthropic_betas` option on a Claude endpoint controls which client-supplied beta values are forwarded:
218	
219	- Unset (default): the header is forwarded unchanged.
220	- An empty list: the header is dropped.
221	- A list of values, for example `["web-search-2025-03-05"]`: only those values are kept, and the header is dropped if none remain.
222	
223	The option is part of the model's Vertex AI configuration, alongside `vertex_project` and `vertex_location`. Through the API, `auth_config` values are strings, so pass the betas as a comma-separated string such as `"web-search-2025-03-05,interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14"`; an empty string drops the header.
224	
225	### Azure OpenAI
226	
227	Azure OpenAI uses the same passthrough as OpenAI with additional configuration:
228	
229	**Base URL:** `http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1`
230	
231	When creating an Azure OpenAI endpoint:
232	
233	1. Select **Azure OpenAI** as the provider
234	2. Enter your Azure endpoint URL
235	3. Enter your Azure API key
236	4. Specify your deployment name
237	
238	```python
239	from openai import OpenAI
240	
241	client = OpenAI(
242	    base_url="http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1",
243	    api_key="dummy",
244	)
245	
246	response = client.chat.completions.create(
247	    model="my-azure-endpoint",
248	    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
249	)
250	```
251	
252	### Databricks Foundation Models
253	
254	Databricks Foundation Models APIs are OpenAI-compatible:
255	
256	**Base URL:** `http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1`
257	
258	When creating a Databricks endpoint:
259	
260	1. Select **Databricks** as the provider
261	2. Enter your Databricks workspace URL
262	3. Enter your Databricks personal access token
263	4. Specify the model endpoint name
264	
265	```python
266	from openai import OpenAI
267	
268	client = OpenAI(
269	    base_url="http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1",
270	    api_key="dummy",
271	)
272	
273	response = client.chat.completions.create(
274	    model="my-databricks-endpoint",
275	    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
276	)
277	```
278	
279	### TypeSafe
280	
281	The TypeSafe passthrough exposes TypeSafe's System One API through the MLflow Gateway. The gateway endpoint name goes in the request body's `model` field; the gateway forwards the request to the configured TypeSafe model with its server-side TypeSafe API key.
282	
283	**Base URL:** `http://localhost:5000/gateway/typesafe/v1`
284	
285	**Supported Endpoints:**
286	
287	- `POST /systemone` - System One structured evaluation
288	
289	```bash
290	curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/typesafe/v1/systemone \
291	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
292	  -d '{
293	    "model": "jev-evaluator",
294	    "state": {
295	      "inputs": {"question": "How do I reset my password?"},
296	      "outputs": "Select Forgot password on the sign-in page."
297	    },
298	    "questions": {
299	      "evaluation": {
300	        "type": "noul",
301	        "instructions": "Does state.outputs answer the question in state.inputs?"
302	      }
303	    }
304	  }'
305	```
306	
307	TypeSafe gateway endpoints are raw System One endpoints, not chat endpoints. Use them for direct System One requests through Gateway-managed credentials. They are separate from MLflow judges that use `make_judge(model="typesafe:/...")`; do not pass a TypeSafe gateway endpoint as `model="gateway:/..."` to `make_judge()`.
308	
309	### Portkey
310	
311	[Portkey](https://portkey.ai) provides a single OpenAI-compatible API.
312	
313	In addition to your Portkey API key, Portkey needs to know which upstream provider
314	to route each request to. Configure one of the following when creating the endpoint:
315	
316	- **Provider Slug**: a [Model Catalog](https://portkey.ai/docs/product/model-catalog)
317	  integration slug prefixed with `@` (e.g. `@openai-prod`), or a bare provider slug
318	  (e.g. `openai`) together with a **Provider API Key** for that provider
319	- **Config ID or JSON**: a saved Portkey config ID (e.g. `pc-xxxx`) or a raw JSON config. This is stored as a secret, since a raw JSON config may embed upstream credentials
320	- Neither, if your model name already embeds the routing target
321	  (e.g. `@openai-prod/gpt-4o`) or your Portkey API key has a default config attached
322	
323	When creating a Portkey endpoint:
324	
325	1. Select **Portkey** as the provider
326	2. Enter your Portkey API key and a routing target as described above
327	3. Enter your Portkey base URL (e.g. `https://api.portkey.ai/v1`)
328	4. Enter the model name as per your Portkey configuration
329	   (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `@openai-prod/gpt-4o`, or a custom alias)
330	
331	```python
332	from openai import OpenAI
333	
334	client = OpenAI(
335	    base_url="http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1",
336	    api_key="dummy",  # Not needed, configured server-side
337	)
338	
339	response = client.chat.completions.create(
340	    model="my-portkey-endpoint",
341	    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
342	)
343	print(response.choices[0].message.content)
344	```
345	
346	See [Portkey documentation](https://portkey.ai/docs) for the full list of supported models and configuration options.
347	
348	## Model Capabilities
349	
350	When creating endpoints, the model selector shows capability badges:
351	
352	| Badge         | Description                                  |
353	| ------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
354	| **Tools**     | Model supports function/tool calling         |
355	| **Reasoning** | Model has enhanced reasoning capabilities    |
356	| **Caching**   | Model supports prompt caching for efficiency |
357	| **Vision**    | Model can process images                     |
358	
359	Additional information displayed:
360	
361	- **Context window**: Maximum tokens the model can process
362	- **Token costs**: Input and output pricing per million tokens
363
